claim: withoutTools gives an unlabeled tool set the heading "<Id> without"

triage.scenario: A set with no `label` is headed by its id, and `withoutTools` renames it `${id}-without`. Pass `withoutTools(SHAPE_TOOLS, 'line')` as `describeShortcuts`' `toolSets` (the form apps/draw passes as stacks) and the group heading becomes `groupTitle('shapes-without')`, which reads "Shapes without". It should still read as the set's own name. A label taken from the original id is missing.
triage.cause: suffixed id leaks into the label fallback

claim: `ToolsApi.hotkeyEngaged` can name another canvas's tool

triage.scenario: `hotkeyEngaged = ctx.hotkeyStack.at(-1)` reads the whole hotkey stack. That stack can sit in a provider shared by several canvases (useTools' own unmount comment says so, and `toolOptionSteps`/`tuneToolOptions` filter it with `liveTool(slot, among)` for this reason). Holding Space on canvas 2's hand tool makes canvas 1's `tools.hotkeyEngaged` read canvas 2's tool id, which is not in canvas 1's `registry`. A palette that does `registry[hotkeyEngaged]` or highlights that id shows the wrong thing. It should be the newest held id that this registry holds, the same answer `liveTool(…, among)` gives. Two answers to one question.
triage.cause: hotkey stack not filtered to own registry

claim: The shadow pass misses a hotkey-tier action that outranks a tool's binding at a different specificity or target

triage.scenario: The shadow check reuses `findConflictsKeyed`, whose buckets include the specificity `rank`, the exact `targetKey`, and the required-modifier count. The dispatcher ranks tier before specificity. So a hotkey-tier action with an untargeted `click` takes every click from a tool's `click` on `empty`, and an action on bare `x` takes Shift+x from a tool whose binding has `mods: { shift: 'optional' }`. Neither case is reported as `shadows`, although the tool's binding fires only when the action declines. Only exact rank and target matches are reported.
triage.cause: within-scope tie keys reused for a cross-tier comparison

claim: A shared number option's widened leaf keeps the first tool's clearable, scale, stops and step, which may not hold over the merged range

triage.scenario: tool A declares shared `size` as `{ min: 1, max: 100, scale: 'log' }`, tool B as `{ min: 0, max: 50, clearable: true }` → the shared leaf is `{ min: 0, max: 100, scale: 'log' }` without `clearable`: B clearing its field writes `undefined`, which the store's `repairNumber` reads as the default, so B can never clear; and the log scale now spans 0, which warns and draws linear. Widening widens bounds only; the other fields that constrain what a value may be are taken from whichever tool came first.
triage.cause: only min/max/endless widened

claim: Releasing a programmatic hotkey hold pops the last same-id entry, removing a later keyboard hold's priority

triage.scenario: Stack A(programmatic), B, A(key); releasing the programmatic A leaves A, B, so B wins while A's key is still down
triage.cause: API stores only the tool id; popHotkey removes the last match

claim: toolOptionsPrefs silently ignores a host shared default whose key no tool names

triage.scenario: a host passes `shared: { fil: '#f00' }` (a typo for `fill`), or a key no mounted tool shares. The loop does `if (!leaf || !('kind' in leaf)) continue;`, so the default is dropped with no error. Every shape's `fill` then starts at the first tool's declared default. A default that a leaf rejects throws in the same function, so one bad host default is reported and the other is not.
triage.cause: unmatched shared key skipped silently

claim: Whether a child's `toolOptionValues` beats the canvas's `values` prop depends on mount order
tuneToolOptions' `readBy` is never cleared, so a panel edit of a run no tool read writes into the last tool that did
`useTools` throws mid-life when the initial `active` tool leaves the registry
phasesTie's 1 << n enumeration overflows at 31+ channels so identical phase lists fail to tie, and blows up near 30

triage.scenario: Two equal-rank bindings with identical phase lists naming 29 channels; with the owner and a sentinel, 1 << 31 is negative, so no state is tested
triage.cause: power-set enumeration with signed 32-bit shift

claim: findScopedConflicts looks up an entry's eligible rule by ownerId, so a tool that shares an id with a gated action inherits that action's rule

triage.scenario: `rules` is keyed by action id, but `ruleOf` reads `rules.get(entry.ownerId)` for every entry, tools and contributions included. A registry/ambient tool `text` beside a gated action `text` (eligible only in mode X) has its bindings treated as gated: two ambient entries colliding with the tool are then excused whenever the action's rule is exclusive with theirs (rulesExclusive / no mode lets both hold), and a real tie goes unreported. The comment says "Only actions carry a rule, so a tool's ... bindings count as eligible always", which the id lookup does not enforce.
triage.cause: tool and action ids share one key space

claim: toolOptionsPrefs throws a misleading "would share one place" error when one tool is listed twice

triage.scenario: a host builds the schema from every tool it mounts, e.g. `toolOptionsPrefs([...Object.values(registry), ...ambient])`. `useTools` explicitly allows the same tool object in both `registry` and `ambient`. On the second visit the tool's group already holds its own option keys, so the check fires: `tool "brush"'s option "size" and the tool "brush.size" would share one place`. The tool is the same object and nothing collides. Expected: a tool seen again under the same id is skipped (or merged idempotently), and the throw is kept for a real option/tool-id collision.
triage.cause: no dedupe of tools by id before placing groups

claim: describeShortcuts merges an action group named `other` into the ungrouped "Other" group

triage.scenario: an action with `group: 'other'` is keyed `'other'`, the same key ungrouped actions use (`action.group ?? OTHER`). Its rows merge with the ungrouped rows under the heading "Other" and move to the end, instead of getting a group of their own (`groupTitle('other')`) in first-registered order. The tool-set side forbids the id `other` and throws, but the command side merges silently, so the two places answer the same reserved-id question in two different ways.
triage.cause: reserved group id shared with user group ids

claim: Stepping `]` (grow) on a sharing brush at its own max shrinks the shared size for every other brush
where: packages/brush/src/brushSize.ts:10 (shareBrushSize — its contract "one size, held to each tool's own bounds"); the write happens in packages/routing/src/tools/toolOptionSteps.ts:39-41 via steppedOption (packages/routing/src/tools/toolOptions.ts)

claim: Ingest bindings with overlapping but different MIME filters are bucketed apart, so real ties go unreported

triage.scenario: Two ambient drop bindings, same target/phase/mods, types ['image/*'] and ['image/png']; dropping a PNG matches both at equal rank, but no tie is reported
triage.cause: conflict key buckets by MIME filter string

claim: A tool redefined under the same id while live never gets `onActivate`, and the old definition never gets `onDeactivate`
A dotted tool id whose parent has no options gets a prefs group with an empty name

triage.scenario: `toolOptionsPrefs([pathBrushTool])` where the id is `path.brush` and no tool `path` has options. The intermediate segment `path` gets a placeholder `{ name: '', children: {} }`, and nothing ever names it. A prefs panel drawing the schema then shows an untitled group holding the brush's options. The group should carry a name, such as the segment itself or the parent tool's label.
triage.cause: placeholder group never named

claim: A panel value clamped to the leaf's default is dropped instead of written
A conflict is lost when another tie among different bindings uses the same spec objects

triage.scenario: the conflict key is built from the gesture, the target, and each member's `identityKeyOf(e.spec)` and modifiers. It has no owner and no binding identity in it. Bindings often share one spec object, such as a module constant like `{ kind: 'key', key: 'Escape' }` or `STEP_KEYS`. Two components in one bucket that don't tie with each other then get the same key. For example, gated actions A and B can hold together in mode M1, C and D in mode M2, A/B and C/D are exclusive, and all four bind the same spec constant. `tieComponents` yields [A,B] and [C,D]. The second reaches `conflicts.get(key)`, only adds its platform, and returns, so C–D is never reported. Both should be reported.
triage.cause: conflict key omits owner/binding identity

claim: `toolGaps` reports "no cursor" for a tool that carries `Tool.cursor` but no `def.cursor`
One conflict can name bindings that do not tie with each other
useToolOptionParams passes values.subscribe to useSyncExternalStore unbound, losing its `this`

triage.scenario: a host implements `ToolOptionValues` as a class whose `subscribe` reads `this` (e.g. `this.listeners.add(l)`). That is valid against the public interface, but `useSyncExternalStore(values.subscribe, …)` calls it with `this` undefined, so the options row throws on mount. Every other call site goes through `values.get(...)` / `values.set(...)` as methods, so only this path breaks. Should pass `(l) => values.subscribe(l)`, memoized on `values`.
triage.cause: method extracted from interface object

claim: Conflict checker misses a `code` spec colliding with a `key` spec for the same physical key
ToolsScope remounts its whole subtree when `isolate` changes or an outer scope appears or disappears
steppedOption can step an off-grid value backwards when the scaled move is smaller than the snap
`disengageHotkey` with no holds of its own pops whatever tops the stack, including a tool held on its key
A shared tool option that is not a number keeps only the first tool's schema, so the store repairs other tools' values away
liveTool picks a held tool that the active mode bars, so tool options and step keys follow a tool that input does not route to

triage.scenario: brush is active, and a tool `eraser` with options is held on its key (`tool.offhand` pushes it onto the hotkey stack with no mode check, `toolOffhand.ts:86`) while the active mode's capabilities bar it. `useContributions`' `routedTool` skips the barred hold and routes input to brush. But `liveTool` returns `eraser`: `tuneToolOptions` tunes brush's action with nothing (its `active()` is false) and the panel shows eraser's options, and `[` / `]` run `enabledFor('brush')`, which declines because `liveFrom` says `eraser`. So while the hold lasts, the brush's options no longer reach its strokes and its size keys do nothing. Both should use the same rule: the newest hold the mode allows, else the active tool if allowed (`ToolsApi.routed`).
triage.cause: two definitions of "the live tool", one ignoring mode eligibility

claim: findScopedConflicts reports one self-collision twice when a group pass joins a third binding to it

triage.scenario: ambient tool T has two bindings on the same tuple, and ambient tool U has a third. The self pass `findConflictsKeyed([T])` reports the conflict {T.b1, T.b2}. The ambient group pass then finds the component {T.b1, T.b2, U.b}, whose `addConflict` key holds three spec identities and whose ownerIds are [T, T, U], so the `seen` dedupe (key + ownerIds) does not match the first. Both get reported, and the [T, T] pair shows up twice in `reportRouteConflicts` output. The same thing happens in the hotkey group for two hotkey-capable registry tools.
triage.cause: dedupe keyed on the whole component, not on the pairs it contains

claim: The shortcut sheet never lists keys a tool binds itself, including the option-step `[` `]` keys
describeShortcuts never lists keys bound through a tool's own bindings (e.g. the `[` `]` option steps)
steppedOption's 12-significant-digit cleanup can move a large value by more than the step

triage.scenario: Step up from 1000000000009 with step 0.2; the result rounds to 1000000000010, a jump of 1
triage.cause: significant-digit cleanup rather than step-relative rounding

claim: findConflicts merges non-transitive ties into one conflict, naming owners that never tie
onSwitch can fire twice for one dropped tool

triage.scenario: the active tool T leaves `entriesById` while `active` still reads `T`. `dropped` is true and `onSwitch` runs (ending T's in-flight handles), and `prevActiveRef` stays `T`. When the slot is later cleared or moved (`active` becomes `null` or U, which a host or the context does after a tool is removed), `switched` is true, so `onSwitch` runs a second time for the same outgoing tool and may end handles the incoming state already started. A drop should record that T's switch has been handled, for example by setting `prevActiveRef` to `null`.
triage.cause: drop path leaves prevActiveRef pointing at the ended tool

claim: Predicate targets bucket by the `{ kindOf }` wrapper's identity, not the predicate function's, so two bindings sharing one function go unflagged
A `times` step on a size option at 0, with no `step` on the leaf, never moves
Holds made through `engageHotkey` survive the unmount of the `useTools` that made them
A tool held on its hotkey has its options tuned in, but its size/strength step keys and Shift+wheel are disabled
useToolOptionValues throws outside a DepRegistryProvider, though its doc promises a silent no-op
describeShortcuts lists a tool's declared bindings without applying binding overrides, so a rebound tool key shows its old shortcut

triage.scenario: a brush tool with `options.size` gets `brush.grow` bound to `]` on the tool's own `bindings` (defineTool → toolOptionSteps). The host rebinds it with `bindingOverrides` (binding id `brush.grow.key` → `=`). At runtime `assemble.ts:28` applies `overriddenBindings(entry.bindings, entry.id, overrides)` to the tool's bindings, so `=` fires. `describeShortcuts(registry.list(), { tools })` merges `tool.bindings` raw, so the sheet still shows `]` (and an unbound one still shows). The file's header promises "a rebound key reads rebound and an unbound one is gone"; the actions half holds because `list()` applied overrides, the tool half does not, and `DescribeShortcutsOptions` has no `overrides` field (describeKeymap and findScopedConflicts both take one).
triage.cause: overrides not applied to tool-declared bindings

claim: A wheel reversal is not seen as a new burst when the burst's leftover travel is exactly 0
A shared number option held at ±Infinity reads as the default instead of being clamped, for a tool whose leaf is not endless

triage.scenario: tools A (size leaf `max: 500, endless: 'max'`) and B (size leaf `max: 500`, no endless) share `size`. A steps size to `Infinity` (steppedOption does this at the endless end). B reads the shared slot: `readHeld` rejects a non-finite number its own leaf does not allow and returns `undefined`, so B's params fall back to B's default (say 10) rather than 500. toolOptionsPrefs documents that "each tool reads it held to its own" bounds, and steppedOption itself treats a non-finite value as at the leaf's max/min; a finite 10_000 would read 500 while Infinity reads 10. Pressing `]` in B then writes `default+step` over A's value.
triage.cause: non-finite rejected before clamping

claim: Re-publishing on every `ToolsApi` change moves an older canvas to newest, so it takes the scoped slot
A hotkey-tier action that shadows an ambient tool's binding is never reported as a conflict, though the same shadow over a registry tool is

triage.scenario: an action with `scope: 'hotkey'` and a default `Escape` binding, and an always-on ambient tool binding `Escape` to its own action. The hotkey tier is walked before ambient, so the ambient binding fires only when the action declines, the exact situation the `shadows` report describes. The shadow loop pairs hotkey actions only with `registry` tools; `ambient` (ambient tools plus ungated actions) is never compared with `hotkeyActions`/`gatedHotkey`, and the hotkey group holds only registry tools. Result: no warning for the ambient case, a `shadows` warning for the identical registry case.
triage.cause: shadow pass limited to registry tools

claim: withToolOptionDefault installs a caller's starting value without checking it against the option's leaf

triage.scenario: a tool hook's caller passes a starting `size: 0` (or a string, or 500) for a leaf with `min: 1, max: 100`. The value becomes `leaf.default` unrepaired. `toolOptionParams` hands that default straight to the action while nothing is held, and `stepOption` starts stepping from it. Every held value goes through `readHeld`/`repairPrefValue`, so only the default path skips bounds and kind checks.
triage.cause: default not repaired against the leaf

claim: Tool option values kept in prefs never read back for a tool id or shared key containing `.`
The tools slot goes empty when the last canvas to publish unmounts, though an earlier canvas is still mounted
A host's default for a shared option is not checked against the widened leaf
Step actions and the options tuning answer "which tool is live" two ways
A tool set or action group with the id `other` swallows the ungrouped rows under its own heading
`has()` admits ambient-only ids that `setActive` rejects, so a mode whose `defaultTool` is an ambient tool throws from an effect
foldPlatformCopies folds away a binding duplicated with `mod` so it is never reported as a conflict, though the same duplicate spelled with `ctrl` is reported

triage.scenario: one owner declares `{ kind: 'key', key: 'z', mods: { mod: true } }` to `history.undo` twice with equal params (or a tool declares the same `mod` binding twice). Both entries are `platformBound` and `sameOutcome`, so the fold keeps one and the bucket drops to 1 member; `addConflict` returns early and nothing is flagged on either platform. The same pair written with `ctrl: true` is not platform-bound, survives the fold, ties on both platforms and is flagged. `findConflicts`' doc says "The same pair tying on both platforms is a plain duplicate and is flagged." The fold is meant only for a `mod` copy against a `ctrl`/`meta` copy of one binding, i.e. pairs whose platform-boundness differs.
triage.cause: fold condition `platformBound(k) || platformBound(e)` should require exactly one to be bound

claim: A conflict's ownerIds can include two bindings that never tie with each other, because tie components are merged transitively

triage.scenario: three tools bind the same key: A with `views: ['x']`, B with `views: ['x','y']`, C with `views: ['y']`. A–B tie in view x and B–C tie in view y, but A and C are never live together (`viewsTie` is false). `tieComponents` takes the transitive closure, so one conflict reports `declared by A, B, C`, and `reportRouteConflicts` warns that "two bindings declare the same … tuple in the same scope". A host told A and C collide may change one of them for nothing. The same happens with `phasesTie` or exclusive `eligible` rules. Reporting the pairs (or maximal cliques) that really tie would be accurate.
triage.cause: transitive closure over a non-transitive tie relation

claim: Tool options treat a held tool the active mode disallows as live, while routing skips it
The wheel-resize burst state lives in the tool definition, so every canvas and registry using that tool shares one burst
A tool with the id `shared` shares one slot with the shared tool options
